subject: Fulfillment & entitlement — procurement sync (Acme Analytics)
message_1_subject: Questions on AWS Marketplace fulfillment & billing flow
message_1_body:
Hi Avery/Ben,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Procurement had a few follow-ups after reviewing the marketplace flow and the SaaS contract language:

1) For metering-based SaaS (per-request), we need a clear statement of how entitlements map to our internal seat/usage model — does Redwood provide an entitlement file that lists product SKU + customer entitlement units per month?
2) Billing cadence: our AP team expects invoice + usage report within 5 business days after month close; can you confirm Redwood or AWS Marketplace will surface the raw usage CSV?
3) Contract redlines: we attached our procurement template — can Redwood confirm any non-negotiable clauses for AWS fulfillment?

We'd also like to confirm whether Redwood will support the marketplace-based proration behavior during initial activation and cancellation.

Can we have a short sync later today to close these items?

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics
maya.patel@acmeanalytics.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

message_2_subject: Re: Questions on AWS Marketplace fulfillment & billing flow
message_2_body:
Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline, and proposing a 30-min sync at 2:15pm PT if that works.

1) Entitlement export: Redwood will provide an entitlement payload (CSV/Excel) that maps our internal SKU IDs to AWS Marketplace product codes. The attached 'SaaS_entitlement_mapping_v3.xlsx' is the draft we discussed — column A = Redwood SKU, column B = AWS product code, column C = units per entitlement. We can export this via the console or push it into your S3 bucket on activation.

2) Billing cadence: For marketplace fulfullment we rely on AWS metering calls for usage reporting. We can surface a daily usage CSV to a signed S3 location (or provide monthly rollups) within 3 business days after month close; AWS finalizes settlements on their timetable but we can provide the raw usage file earlier to your AP team.

3) Contract redlines: Appreciate the procurement template. The PDF shows proposed changes; Ben/Neha have marked two clauses (data residency & audit rights) that will need legal review. The marketplace flow requires a fulfillment clause that allows AWS to act as the billing facilitator — we typically accept minor language adjustments but need to keep the AWS fulfillment delegation intact.

Proration: Redwood supports marketplace-based proration for activation windows and mid-month cancellations; the exact behavior depends on whether you want AWS-managed proration (marketplace handles it) or Redwood-managed proration (we invoice off-marketplace and reconcile). For co-sell customers, we usually recommend AWS-managed proration to keep invoicing centralized.

Proposed sync agenda (30m):
- Confirm entitlement file columns + S3 delivery method (5m)
- Billing file cadence + sample fields (10m)
- Contract redlines that impact marketplace fulfillment (10m)
- Next steps / DocuSign timeline (5m)

Ben/Neha — are you ok to join 2:15pm PT? Maya — does that work on your side?

Thanks,
Avery
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com

---
Attachment notes: SaaS_entitlement_mapping_v3.xlsx (mapping + sample rows); Redlines_Acme_Redwood_2026-08-21.pdf (edits highlighted)
message_3_subject: Re: Questions on AWS Marketplace fulfillment & billing flow — sample CSV and clarifications
message_3_body:
Maya — thanks for confirming a sync. Quick pre-read: attached is a one-week sample usage CSV we send for customer validation (fields: buyer_account_id, aws_product_code, usage_quantity, usage_timestamp, reporting_id).

A few clarifications from engineering ops:
- The entitlement export will be generated by our fulfillment engine nightly and can be pushed to S3 using cross-account role access (we'll need an S3 prefix and a short-lived role ARN).
- For proration, if Acme prefers AWS-managed proration we will not issue a separate prorated invoice off-marketplace; AWS will handle credits via their settlement. If you need our internal delta reports for accounting (some customers do), we can provide reconciled statements within 5 business days.

Next steps before the sync:
- Maya: please share S3 bucket name and whether you want cross-account push or signed upload.
- Acme procurement: confirm if the redlines are 'for discussion' vs 'blocking' — Ben/Neha will feed to Legal.

I'll join the 2:15pm PT sync.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
message_4_subject: Re: Fulfillment & entitlement — procurement sync (Acme Analytics)
message_4_body:
Thanks all — 2:15pm PT works.

S3 details: bucket = acme-exports-us-west-2, preferred approach = cross-account push (we'll create a role for Redwood to assume). I've looped in our procurement mailbox; the redlines are mostly 'for discussion' except clause 12 (audit rights) which is blocking until we get a proposed compromise.

I'll send calendar invite now and include a short pre-read: procurement will need sample CSV columns and an example entitlement mapping (the files you attached look good). Also can you confirm who at Redwood will be the signer for the AWS listing? Our vendor onboarding needs a named contact for the marketplace listing.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — see you at 2:15.

Maya
